facts.title: A 28,000-Year-Old Cave Lion Cub Was Found With Its Whiskers Intact
facts.summary: In 2018, a mammoth tusk hunter in Siberia found a cave lion cub so well preserved that her teeth, skin, claws and whiskers were still intact after about 28,000 years.

facts.title: A Lion's Roar Comes From Flat, Square Vocal Folds
facts.summary: Lions can roar so loudly and deeply because their vocal folds are shaped differently from those of most mammals.

facts.title: A Male Lion Can Eat About 63 Kilograms of Meat in One Meal
facts.summary: A male lion can eat about a quarter of his body weight in a single meal, roughly 140 pounds or 63 kilograms of meat.

facts.title: Asiatic Lions Belong to the Same Subspecies as West African Lions
facts.summary: India's Asiatic lions are no longer treated as a separate subspecies: they share the name Panthera leo leo with the lions of West and Central Africa.

facts.title: Bigger Male Lion Coalitions Hold Their Prides More Than Twice as Long
Herodotus Wrote That Wild Lions Lived in Northern Greece
facts.summary: The ancient Greek historian Herodotus recorded that wild lions lived in northern Greece, and that they attacked the Persian king Xerxes' baggage camels.

facts.title: In Undisturbed Habitats, a Lion's Top Cause of Death Is Other Lions
facts.summary: Where people leave them alone, the biggest threat to a lion is not hunger or disease but other lions.

facts.title: India's Asiatic Lions Rose to 891 in 2025, Most Living Outside Gir
facts.summary: India's wild Asiatic lions reached 891 in the 2025 census, up from 674 five years earlier, and more than half of them now live outside Gir National Park.

facts.title: Lion Attacks on People Spike in the Days After a Full Moon
facts.summary: In Tanzania, lions attack people far more often in the dark evenings that follow a full moon than in the bright nights leading up to it.

facts.title: Lionesses Hunt in Fixed Positions, Like Players on a Team
facts.summary: When lionesses hunt together, many of them play the same role every time, much like players who keep the same position on a sports team.

facts.title: Lionesses Nurse Each Other's Cubs in Shared Nurseries
facts.summary: Lionesses in a pride often raise their cubs together in a group nursery called a creche, and some will even nurse cubs that are not their own.

facts.title: Lionesses Prefer Males With Darker Manes
facts.summary: Female lions in Tanzania's Serengeti are drawn to males with darker manes, and the colour appears to be an honest signal of a male's condition.

facts.title: Lions Can Rest for Up to 21 Hours a Day
facts.summary: Wild lions spend most of their lives doing very little: on average they rest for up to 20 to 21 hours a day.

facts.title: Lions Now Live in About 6% of Their Historical Range
facts.summary: Wild lions survive across only about 6% of the area they once roamed, according to the IUCN Cat Specialist Group.

facts.title: New Male Lions Often Kill the Cubs of the Pride They Take Over
facts.summary: When a new group of males takes over a lion pride, they often kill the young cubs sired by the males they replaced.

facts.title: Only About 250 Adult Lions Remain in West Africa
facts.summary: West Africa's lions are critically endangered, with only about 250 adults left, split among four isolated populations.

facts.title: Some Lionesses in Botswana Grow Manes and Roar Like Males
facts.summary: In Botswana's Okavango Delta, a few wild lionesses have grown manes and taken on behaviour usually seen in males.

facts.title: Tsavo's Man-Eating Lions Probably Ate About 35 People, Not 135
facts.summary: The two lions that terrorised a railway camp at Tsavo, Kenya, in 1898 probably ate about 35 people, far fewer than the legend claims.
